# Overview

This project includes aquatic macroinvertebrate data collected from 
50 streams throughout the Susquehanna River Basin in April 2026, which are used to generate indices of biotic integrity (IBI) scores. IBI scores are used to judge the overall health of a stream and whether human activity is disrupting it.The goal of this project is to explore this dataset and determine the structure of biodiversity throughout the river basin and how it relates to IBI scores.

# Research Questions

1. Do beta diversity metrics change when analyzing at the genus vs. family level?
2. How does diversity relate to IBI scores?
3. Are sites with similar IBI scores also similar in taxa composition?

# Rationale

This data is one part of the dataset that I will be working with for the second chapter of my PhD dissertation. In preparation for the more extensive analysis I will conduct later, I would like to familiarize myself with this data and how community composition is structured throughout the Susquehanna River Basin. I would also like to investigate what factors seem to be most impactful with IBI scores.

# Raw Data

The raw data was provided by the Susquehanna River Basin Commission. There is a single excel file that contains all of the data provided by them as well as several other files that are subsets of the main file. There is also a file with site information.

These are the files currently in `data/raw/`:

```{r raw-file-list}
raw_files <- list.files("data/raw", full.names = TRUE)
knitr::kable(data.frame(file = basename(raw_files),
                        size_kb = round(file.size(raw_files) / 1024, 1)))
```

## File 1: site_data.csv

- Source: Data was produced by the Susquehanna River Basin Commission
- Date accessed: September 1st, 2026
- License or terms of use: This data is public domain
- Citation: Susquehanna River Basin Commission (2026)

This file contains data on each site, including the IBI score calculated from the taxa collected there. Each row represents one site.

```{r read-file-1}
file1 <- read.csv("Data/Raw/site_data.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = "")
```

This file has `r nrow(file1)` rows and `r ncol(file1)` columns. Here are the first few rows:

```{r head-file-1}
knitr::kable(head(file1))
```

And here is the type of each column, as R reads it:

```{r str-file-1}
str(file1)
```

### Data dictionary for site_data.csv

| Variable | Description | Type | Units |
|----------|-------------|------|-------|
| `str_station` | site identifier | text | none |
| `INT_MI_SURVEY_GEN_ID` | site number, primary key | whole number | none |
| `SmallFreestoneIBI` | indices fo biotic integrity (IBI) score calculated using benthic macroinvertebrate data, scores range from 0-100 | number | none |

All other columns can be ignored because they will be removed during the data cleaning process.

## File 2: taxa_data.csv

- Source: Data was produced by the Susquehanna River Basin Commission
- Date accessed: September 1st, 2026
- License or terms of use: This data is public domain
- Citation: Susquehanna River Basin Commission (2026)

This file contains all of the taxonomic information and counts of macroinvertebrates found at each site. Each row represents a taxon found at a site.
```{r read-file-2}
file2 <- read.csv("Data/Raw/taxa_data.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = "")
```

This file has `r nrow(file2)` rows and `r ncol(file2)` columns. Here are the first few rows:

```{r head-file-2}
knitr::kable(head(file2))
```

And here is the type of each column, as R reads it:

```{r str-file-2}
str(file2)
```

### Data dictionary for site_data.csv

| Variable | Description | Type | Units |
|----------|-------------|------|-------|
| `station_id` | site identifier | text | none |
| `waterbody` | name of the waterbody | text | none |
| `coll date` | date that the sample was collected | date | none |
| `PA_TAXON_NAME` | lowest taxonomy the individuals were identified to that matches Pennsylvania's official list of taxa | text | none |
| `count` | number of this taxa found in the sample | whole number | counts |
| `phylum` | phylum name of taxon | text | none |
| `class` | class name of taxon | text | none |
| `order` | order name of taxon | text | none |
| `family` | family name of taxon | text | none |
| `genus` | genus name of taxon | text | none |
| `PA_HILS_ID_LEVEL` | pollution tolerance level, ranges from 0-10 with 0 being the lowest tolerance level | whole number | none |
| `PA_TROPHIC` | functional feeding group codes | text | none |

All other columns can be ignored because they will be removed during the data cleaning process.


# Planned Workflow

## Data cleaning

Currently the data is structured how I would like it to be, which is why many of the columns are not included in the data dictionaries. I will need to completely restructure the data so that there is a site data file that includes site name, waterbody, IBI score, and other related information as well as a file that contains all of the taxonomic information and counts for each taxa found at each site.

## Visualization

Hierarchical clustering will be used to visually assess the relatedness between sites. Additionally, beta diversity will be visualized using bar graphs, as will characteristics such as species richness. Regional differences in IBI scores will also be represented by box plots.

## Analysis

IBI scores will be used as a variable to compare community composition throughout the basin. I will calculate beta diversity metrics throughout the basin as well as ordination to determine if the sites cluster together, and if this clustering is by IBI score.
